A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GradPower. All 22 pages of v2 and 24 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations and appendix proofs, support comparison. Renamed optimizers and renumbered sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model pre-training experiments, optimizer comparisons and batch-size analyses in Section 3, plus numerical simulations in Figure 7.

after.justification: v3 retains original pre-training and simulation results and adds downstream evaluations, CIFAR-10 experiments, clipping-order comparisons and repeated-seed experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.5 introduces AdamWPower-II, a variant applying clipping after the power transformation. The default sign-power transformation and optimizer updates remain unchanged. AdamPower becoming AdamWPower clarifies the decoupled weight decay already used in v2.

E1.justification: v3 adds zero-shot evaluation on ARC-E, ARC-C, PIQA, HellaSwag, OBQA and WinoGrande, plus CIFAR-10 image classification using ResNet-34. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained C4/OpenWebText pre-training experiments and synthetic example.

E2.justification: The new clipping-order comparison evaluates AdamWPower-II alongside AdamW and default AdamWPower in Figure 6. The main comparator families remain unchanged: Adam with decoupled decay, Blockwise LR and Muon. Newly discussed Powerball methods are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: v3 adds zero-shot testing, a vision batch-size/power protocol, clipping-order controls and a 12-configuration momentum sweep. It also revises the reported d_model/d_FF dimensions for LLaMA 0.2B and 0.25B from 768/3072 to 1024/4096 (v2 Table 1; v3 Table 3). This establishes a reported configuration change, without establishing whether those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether clipping order matters, whether gains survive momentum tuning, and whether differences persist across random seeds (Section 4.5; Appendices B.4–B.5). The batch-size analysis also extends to vision. These address substantial robustness questions absent from v2.

E5.justification: v2 provides no repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates. Appendix B.4 explicitly reports six reruns with different seeds for the 66M and 0.2B C4/cos comparisons, displaying means and standard deviations in Figure 8. Figure 6 also identifies standard-deviation shading. Formal significance tests are not reported.

E6.justification: New results include downstream averages of 47.72 for AdamW and 48.26 for AdamWPower (Table 1), CIFAR-10 scores, robustness results, and momentum-tuned losses of 2.832831 versus 2.828666. v3 also reports 0.7534 versus 0.7565 seconds per step and adds FLOP annotations. Section 4.4 corrects the Figure 5 prose gains from 0.45/0.15/0.3 to 0.045/0.015/0.03; these are reporting corrections, not demonstrated performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: v2 Theorem 4.8 claims an expected squared-gradient bound of O(log^(2/(p+1))(T)/T^(1/(p+1))). v3 Theorem 5.8 instead bounds the expected (p+1)-power L_(p+1) gradient by O(log(T)/sqrt(T)), revises the Adam comparison through Jensen's inequality, and removes the original final moment conversion from the proof. EMA normalization and several smaller proof expressions are also corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a lightweight gradient transformation, improved language-model pre-training, compatibility with other optimizers, and noise-dependent theoretical acceleration. Added experiments support these claims without materially changing their stated scope.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly qualifies flat directions as approximately corresponding to small stochastic-gradient directions, explains the connection through noise anisotropy, and acknowledges that direct full-gradient verification in LLMs is infeasible. New analyses also motivate clipping/momentum robustness interpretations, while the conclusion adds adaptive scheduling of p as future work.

D1.justification: v3 adds the evaluation-harness reference, default clipping order, timing measurements, vision learning-rate settings and momentum-search configurations. It revises reported dense-model dimensions and removes v2's statement that sliding-window attention was disabled for MoE experiments. Most existing tokenization, hardware and training-budget information is retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix A acknowledges closely related Powerball/power-gradient work, including prior use with Adam, and positions GradPower around modern LLM optimizers and exploration of p greater than one. It also distinguishes Powerpropagation's parameter transformation. Section 2 substantially expands the noise-geometry literature supporting the mechanism discussion.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains recognizable. Changes include the AdamW naming clarification, grammar corrections, promotion of Related Works to a standalone section, relocation of Notations, and integration of new subsections and appendices. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references. Figure 1 changes from parameter-count to compute axes, Figure 3 is rearranged, Figure 6 gains a clipping panel, and Figure 8 and two result tables are added. Existing configuration tables and appendix material are relocated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important credibility gaps through six-seed replication, momentum/clipping controls, measured overhead and downstream evaluation. Appendix A supplies previously missing attribution to closely related power-gradient methods, while the revised low-noise theorem removes v2's unsupported final moment conversion. These substantially improve empirical support, positioning and theoretical consistency. Replication remains limited to small dense models, and the model-dimension revisions are unexplained, but these limitations do not outweigh the documented gains.
